verdicts.note: Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: use another letter for the digit width (for example w or b) instead of k, since k is the padded length on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If k is kept, say on the page that it means digit width here.

Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: x there is the integer value, while on the exact-integer-multiplication page x is the binary string and val(x) is its integer. Use val(x) for the integer, or another letter for the integer, and keep x for the string where the string is meant.

Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: y there is the integer value, while on the exact-integer-multiplication page y is the binary string and val(y) is its integer. Use val(y) for the integer, or another letter, and keep y for the string where the string is meant.

Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: use another letter (for example p or r) for the coefficient position, since m is the integer argument of bin_k on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If m is kept, say on the page that it is a coefficient position here.

Chinese-remainder-map is the later page: use another letter (for example r) for the number of cyclic axes, since d is the digit count on the radix-digit-convolution page. If d is kept, the page already says it is the axis count and not the digit count.

Chinese-remainder-map is the later page: use another letter (for example p or u) for the cyclic position, since n is the input length on the exact-integer-multiplication page. The map page already flags this; avoid n for the position in any further use.
Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example j or a) for the axis index, since i is the imaginary unit on the gaussian-resampling page.

Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example X or L) for the real padded-length variable, since x is the integer represented by the first input on the radix-digit-convolution page. If x is kept, say here that it is a real padded length, not the integer input.

Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example X or L) for the real padded-length variable, since x is the binary input string on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If x is kept, say here that it is a real padded length, not an input string.
